reuse.why: All sites call the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend (now taking the enable flag and holidays), but the daily-skip rule and the non-working-day test are re-implemented at each server call site instead of using a shared definition (isNonWorkingDay is kept private and re-spelled as d.isWeekend || isHoliday in app.ts).

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend + non-working day -> drop, else shift' block is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), the two app.ts flatMap bodies being near-identical, and schedule-template.ts keeps two identical ternary blocks.

placement.why: Date-adjustment logic belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip policy lives in server/schedules/app.ts handlers and getNextDate rather than in the shared helper.

scope.why: Edits stay on schedule date logic, the new handler, the type and tests; the occurrence over-fetch in getUpcomingDates is a related necessity.

maintainability.why: The weekend/holiday rule is split between a helper and three hand-written daily branches (schedule-template.ts not applying the daily rule at all), so the next rule change must be made in several places that already disagree.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts and getNextDate in shared/schedules.ts decide daily weekend/holiday skipping themselves around getDateWithSkippedWeekend; app.ts re-spells isNonWorkingDay.

disguised_duplication.where: Daily-skip check reshaped as a flatMap filter in getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange and as a retry loop in getNextDate; isNonWorkingDay re-expressed inline as d.isWeekend(date) || isHoliday(...).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gained skipWeekend and holidays parameters plus an early-return branch; getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each carry their own daily-frequency branch outside the helper.
